newsitem.title: USA: Indiana commission to review tax system.
newsitem.headline: Indiana commission to review tax system.

text.p: An Indiana commission has until December 1998 to come up with a new tax system for the state.
Gov. Frank O'Bannon announced the 32-member Citizen's Commission on Taxes on Monday, charging it with bringing "fairness and simplicity to Indiana's complex and confusing patchwork of taxes."

"First and foremost, we must strive for a tax system that is fair," O'Bannon said in a news release. "In particular, Indiana must reduce its reliance on property taxes. That reliance creates severe inequities in school funding. It also imposes hardships on farmers and on homeowners living on fixed incomes."
Recommendations from the commission would be sumitted to the General Assembly for consideration during its 1999 session, O'Bannon said.
In the meantime, he reiterated his call for immediate tax relief through temporary income tax credits.
